1. Fix the dollar change: current total $160.62 ($18.38 + $23.29 + $118.95; meter reads 22,882 − 21,997 = 885 kWh) minus last month $226.04 = −$65.42. Confirm last month was 1,292 kWh over 30 days.

2. Rate component: both periods fall under the same AEP Ohio RS tariff window (2025-01-01 to 2026-04-09), same $18.38 fixed charge, same first-tier variable rate $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh, and both usages are below 2,000 kWh. Set price_usd = 0.00.

3. Days component: the fixed charge is monthly, not prorated, and energy/riders are billed per kWh, so the 31-vs-30 day difference is not a separate tariff charge. Set days_usd = 0.00 and avoid double-counting day effects later.

4. Weather component: use NOAA degree days—last month HDD 1,202/CDD 0 versus current HDD 1,069.5/CDD 0. Derive kWh per HDD/CDD from the bill history while separating baseline non-weather usage, compute weather-attributable kWh change from the HDD difference, and value it at $0.1607225/kWh. Expect weather_usd ≤ 0 because the current period was warmer.

5. Usage component: set usage_usd = −65.42 − price_usd − days_usd − weather_usd so the four parts sum exactly to the total change; this is the residual non-weather household usage difference.

6. Billing-error screen: reconstruct tariff totals for 885 kWh (~$160.62) and 1,292 kWh (~$226.04), verify meter reads, line-item sums, and stated totals; any difference should be only rounding. Set billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null unless a mismatch exceeds rounding. Return only the JSON object with the six required keys.
